name: Frejus
full_name: Fréjus underground nucleon-decay and neutrino experiment
summary: A historical fine-grained iron calorimeter at the Modane Underground Laboratory searched for nucleon decay and studied atmospheric-neutrino interactions and muons.
detection_principle: Alternating iron absorber sheets and flash-tube tracking planes imaged charged-particle topologies. Interleaved Geiger planes triggered the apparatus, allowing neutrino interactions to be distinguished from throughgoing muons.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The founding collaboration reports describe the installed historical apparatus; it is not a present-day Modane detector.

timeline.event: Partial detector began operation in March.

collaboration.name: Frejus Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Readout
key_parameters.value: Approximately 0.93 million flash tubes with 113 Geiger trigger planes

results.summary: Recorded contained atmospheric-neutrino interactions and set nucleon-decay limits; its flavour-ratio precision was lower than later large oscillation experiments.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
